speaker_name: Address by Mr. Mokgweetsi Eric Keabetswe Masisi
speaker_title: Address by Mr. Mokgweetsi Eric Keabetswe Masisi, President of the Republic of Botswana

paragraphs.text: Mr. President,
paragraphs.raw_text: Mr. President,

paragraphs.text: Your Excellencies,
paragraphs.raw_text: Your Excellencies,

paragraphs.text: Distinguished Ladies and Gentlemen,
paragraphs.raw_text: Distinguished Ladies and Gentlemen,

paragraphs.text: I am honoured to address this 75th United Nations General Assembly for the first time since the renewal of my mandate as President of the Republic of Botswana at our General Elections, held on 23 October 2019.
paragraphs.raw_text:
I am honoured to address this 75th United Nations General Assembly for the 
first time since the renewal of my mandate as President of the Republic of Botswana 
at our General Elections, held on 23 October 2019.

paragraphs.text: This Assembly is unique in many ways. It marks the 75th Anniversary of the United Nations, it is virtual, and it is held against the backdrop of the greatest challenge of our time, the COVID-19 pandemic.
paragraphs.raw_text:
This Assembly is unique in many ways. It marks the 75th Anniversary of 
the United Nations, it is virtual, and it is held against the backdrop of the greatest 
challenge of our time, the COVID-19 pandemic.

paragraphs.text: Allow me therefore, to extend our heartfelt condolences and sympathies to families and friends, throughout the world, who have been affected by the pandemic. I also pay special tribute to all those in the frontline of this battle.
paragraphs.raw_text:
Allow me therefore, to extend our heartfelt condolences and sympathies to 
families and friends, throughout the world, who have been affected by the pandemic. 
I also pay special tribute to all those in the frontline of this battle.

paragraphs.text: I am confident that, like other challenges before, we will, together put up a spirited fight against it and emerge wiser, stronger and more resilient in our preparedness to deal with similar pandemics.
paragraphs.raw_text:
I am confident that, like other challenges before, we will, together put 
up a spirited fight against it and emerge wiser, stronger and more resilient in our 
preparedness to deal with similar pandemics.

paragraphs.text: Mr. President,
paragraphs.raw_text: Mr. President,

paragraphs.text: I join other delegations that have spoken before me in congratulating you on your assumption of the Presidency of the 75th Session of the United Nations General Assembly. We welcome the priorities you presented, and pledge my delegation’s full support in the execution of your mandate.
paragraphs.raw_text:
I join other delegations that have spoken before me in congratulating you on 
your assumption of the Presidency of the 75th Session of the United Nations General 
Assembly. We welcome the priorities you presented, and pledge my delegation’s full 
support in the execution of your mandate.

paragraphs.text: Let me also take this opportunity to extend our profound gratitude to your predecessor, His Excellency Professor Tijjani Muhammad-Bande, for his stewardship of the General Assembly during its 74th Session.
paragraphs.raw_text:
Let me also take this opportunity to extend our profound gratitude to your 
predecessor, His Excellency Professor Tijjani Muhammad-Bande, for his stewardship 
of the General Assembly during its 74th Session.

paragraphs.text: Mr. President,
paragraphs.raw_text: Mr. President,

paragraphs.text: Botswana endorses the theme of this General Assembly Session: “The Future we want, the United Nations we need: reaffirming our collective commitment to multilateralism — confronting COVID-19 through effective multilateral action.”
paragraphs.raw_text:
Botswana endorses the theme of this General Assembly Session: “The Future 
we want, the United Nations we need: reaffirming our collective commitment to 
multilateralism — confronting COVID-19 through effective multilateral action.”

paragraphs.text: This theme is a timely reminder of the value and significance of multilateralism as the ultimate framework through which everlasting solutions to existing and emerging global challenges can be attained. Indeed, the world is a much safer and secure place when our nations work together towards collective responses to the complex threats of our time.
paragraphs.raw_text:
This theme is a timely reminder of the value and significance of multilateralism 
as the ultimate framework through which everlasting solutions to existing and 
emerging global challenges can be attained. Indeed, the world is a much safer and 
secure place when our nations work together towards collective responses to the 
complex threats of our time.

paragraphs.text: Now, more than ever before, multilateral action is needed to effectively respond to an urgent global public health crisis of a kind which has not been seen since the Spanish Flu of 1918.
paragraphs.raw_text:
Now, more than ever before, multilateral action is needed to effectively respond 
to an urgent global public health crisis of a kind which has not been seen since the 
Spanish Flu of 1918.

paragraphs.text: We can all agree, that our collective cooperation will be required to repair our nations’ devastated economies and restore the livelihoods of our societies.
paragraphs.raw_text:
We can all agree, that our collective cooperation will be required to repair our 
nations’ devastated economies and restore the livelihoods of our societies.

paragraphs.text: As the foremost multilateral institution, the United Nations and its most noticable specialised agency; the World Health Organisation (WHO), are better
paragraphs.raw_text:
As the foremost multilateral institution, the United Nations and its most 
noticable specialised agency; the World Health Organisation (WHO), are better

paragraphs.text: suited to mobilise action relating to immediate and long-term responses to the COVID-19 pandemic.
paragraphs.raw_text:
suited to mobilise action relating to immediate and long-term responses to the 

COVID-19 pandemic.

paragraphs.text: We have, without a doubt, seen the organisation move swiftly to support national response efforts in vulnerable parts of the world. Most noticeably were the UN “Solidarity flights” that delivered life-saving medical supplies to the neediest around the world.
paragraphs.raw_text:
We have, without a doubt, seen the organisation move swiftly to support 
national response efforts in vulnerable parts of the world. Most noticeably were the 
UN “Solidarity flights” that delivered life-saving medical supplies to the neediest 
around the world.

paragraphs.text: My delegation welcomes the initiatives and urgent response measures undertaken by the UN System, especially the support rendered, through the UN Country Teams, to this global crisis.
paragraphs.raw_text:
My delegation welcomes the initiatives and urgent response measures 
undertaken by the UN System, especially the support rendered, through the UN 
Country Teams, to this global crisis.

paragraphs.text: We particularly appreciate the leadership provided by the UN Secretary- General during this unprecedented time, particularly his call for a global ceasefire, as well as an affordable COVID-19 vaccine that will be accessed by “every person, everywhere.”
paragraphs.raw_text:
We particularly appreciate the leadership provided by the UN Secretary-
General during this unprecedented time, particularly his call for a global ceasefire, 
as well as an affordable COVID-19 vaccine that will be accessed by “every 

person, everywhere.”

paragraphs.text: Mr. President,
paragraphs.raw_text: Mr. President,

paragraphs.text: As we reflect on how to effectively leverage on multilateralism and international cooperation to better tackle the challenges exposed by COVID-19, it is incumbent upon us to also further examine the ways to strengthen the UN’s response capacities.
paragraphs.raw_text:
As we reflect on how to effectively leverage on multilateralism and international 
cooperation to better tackle the challenges exposed by COVID-19, it is incumbent 
upon us to also further examine the ways to strengthen the UN’s response capacities.

paragraphs.text: In doing so, we should also seize the opportunity to re-double our ambition towards attainment of the 2030 Agenda; the future we want. We should galvanize momentum to accelerate SDGs implementation by building on the Secretary General’s wise call for a “Decade of Action”.
paragraphs.raw_text:
In doing so, we should also seize the opportunity to re-double our ambition 
towards attainment of the 2030 Agenda; the future we want. We should galvanize 
momentum to accelerate SDGs implementation by building on the Secretary General’s 
wise call for a “Decade of Action”.

paragraphs.text: 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development
paragraphs.raw_text: 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development

paragraphs.text: Mr. President,
paragraphs.raw_text: Mr. President,

paragraphs.text: The 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, and its Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), constitute a firm blueprint that should continue to guide us in our global and national plans.
paragraphs.raw_text:
The 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, and its Sustainable 
Development Goals (SDGs), constitute a firm blueprint that should continue to guide 
us in our global and national plans.

paragraphs.text: We in Botswana remain committed to accelerate our efforts towards the attainment of SDGs during this remaining ‘Decade of Action.’
paragraphs.raw_text:
We in Botswana remain committed to accelerate our efforts towards the 
attainment of SDGs during this remaining ‘Decade of Action.’

paragraphs.text: To realize this ambition, my Government is resolute in the transformation of Botswana’s economy from one that largely relies on the extractive industry, which is vulnerable to globe shocks, to a knowledge-based economy.
paragraphs.raw_text:
To realize this ambition, my Government is resolute in the transformation of 
Botswana’s economy from one that largely relies on the extractive industry, which is 
vulnerable to globe shocks, to a knowledge-based economy.

paragraphs.text: To this end, my Government has introduced economic policy reforms to stimulate and fast-track transformation in many sectors. These actions are aimed at creating an enabling environment for private sector development in pursuit of Goal 8, that is, Decent work and Economic Growth.
paragraphs.raw_text:
To this end, my Government has introduced economic policy reforms to 
stimulate and fast-track transformation in many sectors. These actions are aimed 
at creating an enabling environment for private sector development in pursuit of 

Goal 8, that is, Decent work and Economic Growth.

paragraphs.text: Mr. President
paragraphs.raw_text: Mr. President

paragraphs.text: As I alluded, in Botswana, like in many countries, the pandemic has had farreaching impact on our lives and livelihoods.
paragraphs.raw_text:
As I alluded, in Botswana, like in many countries, the pandemic has had far-
reaching impact on our lives and livelihoods.

paragraphs.text: For our already vulnerable health sector, the pandemic joins a list of challenges, which include: child mortality; non communicable diseases; and HIV and AIDS.
paragraphs.raw_text:
For our already vulnerable health sector, the pandemic joins a list of challenges, 
which include: child mortality; non communicable diseases; and HIV and AIDS.

paragraphs.text: In responding to the escalating rate of Non-Communicable Diseases, my Government has adopted the Multi-sectoral strategy for Prevention and Control of
paragraphs.raw_text:
In responding to the escalating rate of Non-Communicable Diseases, my 
Government has adopted the Multi-sectoral strategy for Prevention and Control of

paragraphs.text: NCDs for 2018-2023. The strategy focuses on prevention measures and enhancing the quality of life for those affected.
paragraphs.raw_text:
NCDs for 2018-2023. The strategy focuses on prevention measures and enhancing the 
quality of life for those affected.

paragraphs.text: Our longstanding battle against HIV and AIDS remains a key priority for my Government. In this context, I am happy to inform that Botswana is well on track to achieve the Joint United Nations Programme on HIV and AIDS 90-90-90 UNAIDS’s treatment target. So far, 86 per cent of people living with HIV have tested and know their status. And of those who know, 83 per cent are on treatment and 90 per cent are virally suppressed.
paragraphs.raw_text:
Our longstanding battle against HIV and AIDS remains a key priority for my 
Government. In this context, I am happy to inform that Botswana is well on track to 
achieve the Joint United Nations Programme on HIV and AIDS 90-90-90 UNAIDS’s 
treatment target. So far, 86 per cent of people living with HIV have tested and know 
their status. And of those who know, 83 per cent are on treatment and 90 per cent are 
virally suppressed.

paragraphs.text: Mr. President
paragraphs.raw_text: Mr. President

paragraphs.text: Botswana is accelerating access to inclusive, equitable quality education through, amongst other interventions, the implementation of the Education and Training Sector Strategic Plan. The ETSSP, as it’s commonly known, aims to transform learning by ensuring access, retention, and promoting life-long learning and skills development.
paragraphs.raw_text:
Botswana is accelerating access to inclusive, equitable quality education 
through, amongst other interventions, the implementation of the Education and 
Training Sector Strategic Plan. The ETSSP, as it’s commonly known, aims to 
transform learning by ensuring access, retention, and promoting life-long learning 
and skills development.

paragraphs.text: Poverty Eradication
paragraphs.raw_text: Poverty Eradication

paragraphs.text: Mr. President
paragraphs.raw_text: Mr. President

paragraphs.text: It is noted that before the pandemic, an estimated 783 million people were living in extreme poverty globally. However, as at June 2020, the World Bank projected that the pandemic could push an additional 71 million people into extreme poverty in 2020, therefore reversing the gains made in recent decades.
paragraphs.raw_text:
It is noted that before the pandemic, an estimated 783 million people were 
living in extreme poverty globally. However, as at June 2020, the World Bank 
projected that the pandemic could push an additional 71 million people into extreme 
poverty in 2020, therefore reversing the gains made in recent decades.

paragraphs.text: Certainly, this turn of events demands our urgent collective action if we are to eradicate poverty in all its multi-dimensional forms everywhere, and for everyone affected, by 2030.
paragraphs.raw_text:
Certainly, this turn of events demands our urgent collective action if we are 
to eradicate poverty in all its multi-dimensional forms everywhere, and for everyone 
affected, by 2030.

paragraphs.text: For its part, my Government will continue to empower and uplift the poor through a variety of the poverty eradication programmes. These programmes equip and enable beneficiaries to start micro and small scale enterprises for better survival. Such programmes have uplifted beneficiaries from poverty through sustainable income generation, creation and sustenance.
paragraphs.raw_text:
For its part, my Government will continue to empower and uplift the poor 
through a variety of the poverty eradication programmes. These programmes equip 
and enable beneficiaries to start micro and small scale enterprises for better survival. 
Such programmes have uplifted beneficiaries from poverty through sustainable 
income generation, creation and sustenance.

paragraphs.text: Mr. President,
paragraphs.raw_text: Mr. President,

paragraphs.text: My delegation notes the unfortunate global increase in violence against women and girls amid the current health crisis. As countries went into lockdowns and people stayed home, many women and girls, regrettably, became an easy target of human predators and were subjected to Gender Based Violence (GBV). This trend goes against the aspirations of Goal 5: Gender Equality and requires our strenuous and collective action.
paragraphs.raw_text:
My delegation notes the unfortunate global increase in violence against 
women and girls amid the current health crisis. As countries went into lockdowns 
and people stayed home, many women and girls, regrettably, became an easy target 
of human predators and were subjected to Gender Based Violence (GBV). This trend 
goes against the aspirations of Goal 5: Gender Equality and requires our strenuous 
and collective action.

paragraphs.text: While the GBV scourge had already been a concern in Botswana, it increased alarmingly during the COVID-19 crisis. To address this problem, my Government has intensified the implementation of the National Strategy towards Ending Gender Based Violence.
paragraphs.raw_text:
While the GBV scourge had already been a concern in Botswana, it increased 
alarmingly during the COVID-19 crisis. To address this problem, my Government 
has intensified the implementation of the National Strategy towards Ending Gender 
Based Violence.

paragraphs.text: Botswana’s Response to COVID-19
paragraphs.raw_text: Botswana’s Response to COVID-19

paragraphs.text: Mr. President,
paragraphs.raw_text: Mr. President,

paragraphs.text: As I stated, COVID-19 has been detrimental to Botswana’s economy. The suspension of international travel and the global economic meltdown have dealt a
paragraphs.raw_text:
As I stated, COVID-19 has been detrimental to Botswana’s economy. The 
suspension of international travel and the global economic meltdown have dealt a

paragraphs.text: heavy blow on the two mainstays of our economy; tourism and diamond mining. The repeated lockdowns and other COVID-19 protocols have also significantly reduced economic activity.
paragraphs.raw_text:
heavy blow on the two mainstays of our economy; tourism and diamond mining. The 
repeated lockdowns and other COVID-19 protocols have also significantly reduced 
economic activity.

paragraphs.text: In its response, my Government availed an economic relief package to support the economy and complement disease containment measures.
paragraphs.raw_text:
In its response, my Government availed an economic relief package to support 
the economy and complement disease containment measures.

paragraphs.text: The Government is now working on an “Economic Recovery and Transformation Plan” that is intended to support the restoration of economic activity; facilitate economic growth; accelerate economic transformation; and build a resilient of the economy.
paragraphs.raw_text:
The Government is now working on an “Economic Recovery and 
Transformation Plan” that is intended to support the restoration of economic activity; 
facilitate economic growth; accelerate economic transformation; and build a resilient 
of the economy.

paragraphs.text: Whereas our economy has been disrupted, Government remains strongly committed to its pre-COVID-19 sustainable development-oriented policies and programs. The Economic Recovery and Transformation Plan will thus add impetus to implementation of these initiatives.
paragraphs.raw_text:
Whereas our economy has been disrupted, Government remains strongly 
committed to its pre-COVID-19 sustainable development-oriented policies and 
programs. The Economic Recovery and Transformation Plan will thus add impetus 
to implementation of these initiatives.

paragraphs.text: COVID-19 and Multilateral Action
paragraphs.raw_text: COVID-19 and Multilateral Action

paragraphs.text: Mr. President,
paragraphs.raw_text: Mr. President,

paragraphs.text: As is evident with any global problem, Nation-States do not have the capacity to address the COVID-19 pandemic and its effects, on their own. A multilateral response is without question, imperative. We therefore echo the call for a rule based and inclusive multilateralism that is open to the voices of civil society, the private sector, and academia as key stakeholders and partners, in shaping the global response.
paragraphs.raw_text:
As is evident with any global problem, Nation-States do not have the capacity 
to address the COVID-19 pandemic and its effects, on their own. A multilateral 
response is without question, imperative. We therefore echo the call for a rule based 
and inclusive multilateralism that is open to the voices of civil society, the private 
sector, and academia as key stakeholders and partners, in shaping the global response.

paragraphs.text: For Botswana, an ideal multilateral response will be one that has short and long-term perspectives. In the short-term, there is a need to provide immediate relief and safety nets to vulnerable countries and peoples. For the long term, post COVID 19 recovery multilateral efforts are needed to provide comprehensive support to the most vulnerable countries and populations.
paragraphs.raw_text:
For Botswana, an ideal multilateral response will be one that has short and 
long-term perspectives. In the short-term, there is a need to provide immediate relief 
and safety nets to vulnerable countries and peoples. For the long term, post COVID 
19 recovery multilateral efforts are needed to provide comprehensive support to the 
most vulnerable countries and populations.

paragraphs.text: My delegation thus welcomes the idea of a recovery that is focused on building back better, faster and even greener and fostering resilience. This is ever so critical for countries emerging from conflict and other humanitarian crises, as well as those still living under unfortunate conditions of foreign occupation.
paragraphs.raw_text:
My delegation thus welcomes the idea of a recovery that is focused on building 
back better, faster and even greener and fostering resilience. This is ever so critical 
for countries emerging from conflict and other humanitarian crises, as well as those 
still living under unfortunate conditions of foreign occupation.

paragraphs.text: Of keen interest to Botswana will also be support given to countries in special situations such as Least Developed Countries; Landlocked Developing Countries; and Small Island Developing States as the most vulnerable category of United Nations Member States. Being a landlocked country, Botswana has, during this pandemic experienced some challenges with cross-border movement of goods and services due to border closures.
paragraphs.raw_text:
Of keen interest to Botswana will also be support given to countries in special 
situations such as Least Developed Countries; Landlocked Developing Countries; and 
Small Island Developing States as the most vulnerable category of United Nations 
Member States. Being a landlocked country, Botswana has, during this pandemic 
experienced some challenges with cross-border movement of goods and services due 
to border closures.

paragraphs.text: In this context, we call for an accelerated effort in the implementation of the Vienna Programme of Action, the Istanbul Program of Action and the SAMOA Pathway, which are designed to ameliorate the challenges faced by these groups of countries.
paragraphs.raw_text:
In this context, we call for an accelerated effort in the implementation of 
the Vienna Programme of Action, the Istanbul Program of Action and the SAMOA 
Pathway, which are designed to ameliorate the challenges faced by these groups 

of countries.

paragraphs.text: For the UN’s multilateral framework to be effective in dealing with the COVID-19 pandemic and other challenges, we need a United Nations that is nimble, agile and fit for purpose. Indeed, since the crisis started, we have seen the Secretariat demonstrating these organisational qualities in its response.
paragraphs.raw_text:
For the UN’s multilateral framework to be effective in dealing with the 
COVID-19 pandemic and other challenges, we need a United Nations that is nimble, 
agile and fit for purpose. Indeed, since the crisis started, we have seen the Secretariat 
demonstrating these organisational qualities in its response.

paragraphs.text: Though the jury is still out on the reforms, my delegation observes that the Management Reforms have brought about some improvements to the organisation’s crisis response. We nonetheless believe more remains to be done, and we encourage the General Assembly and other principal organs to step up their own reform efforts.
paragraphs.raw_text:
Though the jury is still out on the reforms, my delegation observes that the 
Management Reforms have brought about some improvements to the organisation’s 
crisis response. We nonetheless believe more remains to be done, and we encourage 
the General Assembly and other principal organs to step up their own reform efforts.

paragraphs.text: Climate Change
paragraphs.raw_text: Climate Change

paragraphs.text: Mr. President,
paragraphs.raw_text: Mr. President,

paragraphs.text: While COVID-19 is a devastating pandemic, which caught the world unaware and ill-prepared, Climate Change is a phenomenon we are well aware of, and can mitigate against its repercussions. We long declared Climate Change an existential threat, and committed to restrain its rapid devastation. We should therefore re-double our efforts to mitigate its negative effects.
paragraphs.raw_text:
While COVID-19 is a devastating pandemic, which caught the world unaware 
and ill-prepared, Climate Change is a phenomenon we are well aware of, and can 
mitigate against its repercussions. We long declared Climate Change an existential 
threat, and committed to restrain its rapid devastation. We should therefore re-double 
our efforts to mitigate its negative effects.

paragraphs.text: Botswana, a semi-arid country with erratic rainfall and frequent droughts, attaches great importance to Goal 13 (Climate Action). These climatic conditions affect livelihoods by impeding food production. Moreover, recent droughts have resulted in the drying up of water sources including for wildlife. This has contributed to animal deaths and the escalation of the human-wildlife conflict.
paragraphs.raw_text:
Botswana, a semi-arid country with erratic rainfall and frequent droughts, 
attaches great importance to Goal 13 (Climate Action). These climatic conditions 
affect livelihoods by impeding food production. Moreover, recent droughts have 
resulted in the drying up of water sources including for wildlife. This has contributed 
to animal deaths and the escalation of the human-wildlife conflict.

paragraphs.text: In order to strengthen mitigation and adaptation, my Government is developing a Climate Change Response Policy and a National Adaptation Plan. Working with civil society, academia, and international partners, we are accelerating our implementation of our commitments under the Paris Agreement.
paragraphs.raw_text:
In order to strengthen mitigation and adaptation, my Government is developing 
a Climate Change Response Policy and a National Adaptation Plan. Working with civil 
society, academia, and international partners, we are accelerating our implementation 
of our commitments under the Paris Agreement.

paragraphs.text: Human Rights
paragraphs.raw_text: Human Rights

paragraphs.text: Mr. President,
paragraphs.raw_text: Mr. President,

paragraphs.text: Botswana fully subscribes to the three mutually reinforcing pillars upon which the United Nations was founded. We hold firm that the promotion and protection of human rights, democracy, and the rule of law are critical to sustainable development, peace and security.
paragraphs.raw_text:
Botswana fully subscribes to the three mutually reinforcing pillars upon which 
the United Nations was founded. We hold firm that the promotion and protection of 
human rights, democracy, and the rule of law are critical to sustainable development, 
peace and security.

paragraphs.text: Mr President,
paragraphs.raw_text: Mr President,

paragraphs.text: I also wish to take this occasion to reaffirm Botswana’s support for the Human Rights Council on its extensive work in adopting outcomes that advance the global human rights agenda.
paragraphs.raw_text:
I also wish to take this occasion to reaffirm Botswana’s support for the Human 
Rights Council on its extensive work in adopting outcomes that advance the global 
human rights agenda.

paragraphs.text: International Peace and Security
paragraphs.raw_text: International Peace and Security

paragraphs.text: Mr. President,
paragraphs.raw_text: Mr. President,

paragraphs.text: My delegation applauds the United Nation’s continued efforts to maintain global peace and security in the midst of a pandemic. We welcome the Secretary- General’s Appeal for Global Ceasefire and its intended effort of halting armed conflict to allow the world to focus on the more pressing and bigger battle against the pandemic.
paragraphs.raw_text:
My delegation applauds the United Nation’s continued efforts to maintain 
global peace and security in the midst of a pandemic. We welcome the Secretary-
General’s Appeal for Global Ceasefire and its intended effort of halting armed 
conflict to allow the world to focus on the more pressing and bigger battle against 
the pandemic.

paragraphs.text: Also commendable is the COVID-19 Global Humanitarian Response Plan which is designed to provide relief to the most vulnerable groups particularly in conflict affected and low income countries. There is however a need for partnerships and more donor funding for the effective operationalisation of this important plan.
paragraphs.raw_text:
Also commendable is the COVID-19 Global Humanitarian Response Plan 
which is designed to provide relief to the most vulnerable groups particularly in 
conflict affected and low income countries. There is however a need for partnerships 
and more donor funding for the effective operationalisation of this important plan.

paragraphs.text: Mr. President,
paragraphs.raw_text: Mr. President,

paragraphs.text: Turning now to peace and stability in the Southern African region, I note that while it remains relatively stable, there is an emerging threat to peace and security, due to increasing acts of terrorism and insurgency.

As the current Chair of the SADC Organ on Politics, Defence and Security Cooperation, Botswana is committed to ensure that close attention is given to the imperative to combat terrorism and other security threats in order to enhance peace and stability in the SADC region.
paragraphs.raw_text:
As the current Chair of the SADC Organ on Politics, Defence and Security 
Cooperation, Botswana is committed to ensure that close attention is given to the 
imperative to combat terrorism and other security threats in order to enhance peace 
and stability in the SADC region.

paragraphs.text: Mr. President,
paragraphs.raw_text: Mr. President,

paragraphs.text: It has been indisputably established that terrorism knows no borders. It remains a serious threat to international peace and security. Essentially, Botswana remains deeply committed to combating terrorism in all its forms. We thus continue to take the necessary steps to prevent and combat this scourge. This includes the strengthening our Anti-Money Laundering and Counter Terrorism Financing regime. This is testimony to our firm commitment to contribute towards bolstering the integrity and security of the global financial system.
paragraphs.raw_text:
It has been indisputably established that terrorism knows no borders. It 
remains a serious threat to international peace and security. Essentially, Botswana 
remains deeply committed to combating terrorism in all its forms. We thus continue 
to take the necessary steps to prevent and combat this scourge. This includes the 
strengthening our Anti-Money Laundering and Counter Terrorism Financing regime. 
This is testimony to our firm commitment to contribute towards bolstering the 
integrity and security of the global financial system.

paragraphs.text: We appreciate the support provided by the United Nations Office for Counter- Terrorism and other partners, to enhance the capacity of Botswana’s newly established Counter Terrorism Analysis and Fusion Agency in order to enable us to mitigate the exposure to this menace.
paragraphs.raw_text:
We appreciate the support provided by the United Nations Office for Counter-
Terrorism and other partners, to enhance the capacity of Botswana’s newly established 
Counter Terrorism Analysis and Fusion Agency in order to enable us to mitigate the 
exposure to this menace.

paragraphs.text: In conclusion, I wish to reaffirm Botswana’s commitment to, and belief in multilateralism and international cooperation as an indispensable mechanism for fostering peace and security, promoting human rights and sustainable development.
paragraphs.raw_text:
In conclusion, I wish to reaffirm Botswana’s commitment to, and belief in 
multilateralism and international cooperation as an indispensable mechanism for 
fostering peace and security, promoting human rights and sustainable development.

paragraphs.text: It is beyond the shadow of doubt that the United Nations remains more relevant now than it was 75 years ago. This is in view of the complex and multi-faceted challenges confronting humanity today.
paragraphs.raw_text:
It is beyond the shadow of doubt that the United Nations remains more relevant 
now than it was 75 years ago. This is in view of the complex and multi-faceted 
challenges confronting humanity today.

paragraphs.text: Inevitably, the lessons from the COVID-19 pandemic and many others, will become a key determinant of the model of the real future we want and the United Nations we need to recover faster and build a more peaceful, just, and prosperous world for the future generation!
paragraphs.raw_text:
Inevitably, the lessons from the COVID-19 pandemic and many others, will 
become a key determinant of the model of the real future we want and the United 
Nations we need to recover faster and build a more peaceful, just, and prosperous 
world for the future generation!

paragraphs.text: I thank you for your attention.
paragraphs.raw_text: I thank you for your attention.
